title: Presentation of a ringed-topos morphism by ringed sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative rings $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$. Let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ be a morphism of topoi, meaning an adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ whose left adjoint preserves finite limits, and give a ring-sheaf map $f^\sharp:f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$. Then there are small sites $\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ with finite limits, equivalences of topoi $g:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')$ and $e:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D')$, and a morphism of ringed sites $h$ induced by a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor $v:\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$, such that $e\circ f$ and $h\circ g$ are naturally isomorphic as morphisms of ringed topoi. Here $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C'}=g_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'}=e_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$; the ring maps of $g$ and $e$ are the canonical isomorphisms, and $h^\sharp:h^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal D'}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal C'}$. Continuous functors and morphisms of sites mean [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and ring-module sheaves mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Apply the finite-limit generator and prescribed-site comparison constructions to the inverse-image functor. The resulting sites have strong precoverages, finite limits, equivalences and a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor v; cover preservation and the direct-image natural isomorphism are obtained from the generator Hom formulas and the original adjunction.

Form the direct image R supplied by the continuous functor and the composite inverse image H. Conjugating the original adjunction through the two equivalences gives H ⊣ R and an inverse-image comparison α.

Invoke the fixed-square ring and module transport theorem on H, R, α. It supplies the transported commutative ring sheaves, all three RingedToposMorphism structures, their module direct images, the canonical counit ring equations and the final structural-map equality.
The direct functors of the two equivalences are equivalences; rewrite by the equalities supplied by the transport theorem and synthesize the equivalence instances.
